author: Cook, Haruko Taya; Cook, Theodore F.
title: Japan at War: An Oral History
notes: Sixty-odd Japanese people — soldiers, sailors, pilots, nurses, factory workers, colonists, a survivor of the Nanjing garrison, survivors of the firebombing — interviewed in the late 1980s about the war they had lived through. Filed at the memoir rung because that is what it is: testimony given forty-five years after the event, cited for what a person says they saw and believed and never as evidence for a time, a strength or a position. It is here because the sourced vignette is the instrument ADR 0019 says will have to carry what the no-gore rule keeps off the screen, and because a vignette needs a voice. Verified against catalogue records only; no ISBN is recorded.
